title: AdaParse: An Adaptive Parallel PDF Parsing and Resource Scaling Engine
problem: Building trillion-token scientific text datasets for LLM pre-training requires parsing millions of PDFs, but state-of-the-art high-quality parsers (e.g., Nougat) can only process 1-2 PDFs/second on a 4-A100 node, while lightweight parsers produce poor quality on complex documents.
motivation: Different PDFs have vastly different parsing difficulty; routing simpler documents to cheap extraction tools and only complex ones to expensive ML-based parsers (Nougat) can achieve high throughput with comparable accuracy, but requires a document-adaptive routing strategy aligned with human preference.
method: AdaParse implements a hierarchical three-stage classifier pipeline: CLS I (rule-based validity check on PyMuPDF-extracted text features), CLS II (metadata-driven regression predicting if improvement is likely), CLS III (LLM-based multi-class parser selection). Human preferences are collected from 23 domain experts and incorporated via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to fine-tune the SciBERT-based classifier. Parsl orchestrates parallel execution on HPC (Polaris), batching PDFs, warm-starting ML parsers, and distributing tasks across nodes.
key_novelty: DPO-aligned adaptive PDF parser routing that combines a fast text extraction first-pass with hierarchical ML classifiers, aligned to expert human preferences, achieving 17x throughput improvement over Nougat alone with 0.2% better BLEU accuracy.
contributions: Comprehensive benchmark of 7 parsers across 25,000 PDFs with human preference collection from 23 domain experts
DPO-based alignment of parser selection model with human judgment for scientific document quality
Hierarchical classification pipeline (rule-based + metadata regression + LLM-based) for adaptive parser routing
17x throughput improvement vs Nougat with 0.2% better BLEU; scales to ~78 PDFs/sec on 128 Polaris nodes

metrics.speedup: 17x throughput improvement vs Nougat (state-of-the-art parser); ~78 PDF/sec at 128 nodes vs ~8 PDF/sec for Nougat
metrics.accuracy: BLEU 52.1 vs Nougat 48.1 (+0.2% better); 76.9% accepted token rate vs 69.8% Nougat
metrics.other: Evaluated on Polaris HPC (560 nodes, 4x A100 per node); 1000-document held-out benchmark

limitations: Limited to 5% allocation of documents to high-quality (Nougat) parser by design; DPO requires initial human preference collection effort; BLEU score shown to be only partially predictive of human preferences (R^2=46.5%).
